newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schaeuble-Germany will reform taxes by 2000-paper.
newsitem.headline: Schaeuble-Germany will reform taxes by 2000-paper.

text.p: Germany will reform its tax system by the year 2000 despite setbacks to the government's national tax bill this week, Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats said on Friday.
"Tax reform will come," Schaeuble told the mass circulation daily Bild newspaper. "If not now, then at the latest by the year 2000."
The newspaper said Schaeuble expected the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) would find a suitable compromise with the government in a second round of mediation on the reform plans.

Kohl's government on Thursday promised to fight on to push through sweeping tax reform legislation after the 30 billion mark ($16.3 billion) tax-cutting package bill was quashed in a mediation committee in the early hours of Thursday morning.
Schaeuble said he was sure the SPD would soon be ready to strike a deal.

"When it becomes clear to the people that the SPD is consciously blocking efforts to bring down unemployment just so that it can make itself out as the 'saviour in an emergency' at the next election, the SPD will very quickly be ready for an agreement," Schaueble told the newspaper.
